name: Hong Kong
brief: The Hong Kong dollar is pegged to the US dollar, so local interest rates such as HIBOR tend to track US rates. Property and banks are rate-sensitive. Mainland China growth and Stock Connect flows drive large parts of the market, and the main index is heavy in financials and tech.

name: Mainland China
brief: Policy announcements and central bank (PBoC) actions often drive sentiment. The yuan is managed. The property sector and local demand are key swing factors; watch for stimulus signals and credit conditions. Mainland markets are closed 1 to 7 October for Golden Week, so data is as of 30 September.

name: United States
brief: The Federal Reserve, inflation and jobs data, Treasury yields and the dollar set the global tone. Large tech companies dominate index moves. US rate moves transmit abroad through the dollar and capital flows.

name: Japan
brief: Bank of Japan policy and the yen are central. A stronger yen can pressure exporters; yen moves interact with global carry trades. Banks are sensitive to domestic rate changes.

name: United Kingdom
brief: Bank of England policy, gilt yields and sterling drive the market. The FTSE 100 is heavy in energy, miners, banks and global earners, so a weaker pound tends to lift the index.
news_query: "FTSE 100" OR "Bank of England" OR "gilt yields" OR sterling

name: Euro area
brief: The ECB sets policy for the whole euro area; Bund yields and the euro are the key prices. The Euro Stoxx 50 is weighted to industrials, banks and luxury goods, and energy import costs matter.
news_query: "Euro Stoxx" OR "European Central Bank" OR "euro zone economy" OR "Bund yields"

name: India
brief: RBI policy and the rupee matter most; foreign portfolio flows drive large moves. The Nifty is heavy in financials and IT services exporters. India imports most of its oil, so oil prices weigh on it.
news_query: Nifty OR Sensex OR "Reserve Bank of India" OR rupee

name: South Korea
brief: The Bank of Korea and the won set local conditions. The KOSPI is dominated by semiconductors and exporters, so it follows the global chip cycle and Chinese demand.
news_query: KOSPI OR "Bank of Korea" OR "Korean won"

name: Taiwan
brief: The TAIEX is dominated by semiconductors, above all TSMC, so US tech demand and export controls drive it. The central bank manages the Taiwan dollar.
news_query: "Taiwan stocks" OR TAIEX OR "Taiwan dollar" OR TSMC

name: Singapore
brief: MAS runs monetary policy through the Singapore dollar exchange rate rather than an interest rate. The STI is heavy in banks and REITs, which are rate-sensitive.
news_query: "Straits Times Index" OR "Monetary Authority of Singapore" OR "Singapore dollar"

name: Australia
brief: The RBA and the Australian dollar set local conditions. The ASX 200 is heavy in banks and miners, so commodity prices and Chinese demand drive it.
news_query: "ASX 200" OR "Reserve Bank of Australia" OR "Australian dollar"

name: Brazil
brief: Brazil's central bank keeps real interest rates high. The Ibovespa is heavy in commodities and banks, and the real is sensitive to US rates and global risk appetite.
news_query: Ibovespa OR "Brazil central bank" OR "Brazilian real"

name: Canada
brief: The Bank of Canada often moves with the Fed. The TSX is heavy in banks, energy and materials, so oil prices and US demand matter.
news_query: TSX OR "Bank of Canada" OR "Canadian dollar"

name: Saudi Arabia
brief: The riyal is pegged to the US dollar, so Saudi rates follow Fed moves. The Tadawul is heavy in energy, banks and petrochemicals; oil prices dominate.

idx: iShares MSCI Saudi Arabia ETF (index proxy)

news_query: Tadawul OR "Saudi stocks" OR "Saudi Aramco shares"
